newsitem.title: USA: CFTC gets record number letters on CBOT proposal.
newsitem.headline: CFTC gets record number letters on CBOT proposal.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade's controversial proposal to change the delivery terms of its big soybean and corn contracts has drawn comments from more than 600 farm groups, congressmen, shippers and state politicians, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Monday.

Monday marked the deadline for letters to be submitted to the agency, but a CFTC spokesman said any letters postmarked by June 16 but received later in the week would be considered by the commissioners.
Most of the 633 comment letters received by the CFTC so far oppose the exchange's proposal to drop Toledo and replace it with a series of delivery terminals along the northern Illinois river.
"We expect to end the week with somewhere around 650 comment letters," the CFTC spokesman said.

More than two dozen members of the U.S. House of Representatives have expressed their concern about the proposal to the CFTC, along with Sens. Richard Lugar (R-Ind), John Glenn (D-Oh), Mike DeWine (R-Oh), and state leaders from Ohio and Michigan.
Illinois Sen. Carol Mosely-Braun has been one of the few politicians to support the CBOT's plan.
At a rare public hearing on the issue last week, the CFTC gave no indication of quickly it would act on the proposal. The agency can accept the CBOT's plan, or reject it and impose one of its own.

CBOT said the proposed changes would result in a better futures contract that reflects changes in the marketplace and the needs of grain buyers and processors. But opponents claim dropping the port of Toledo would mean concentrate too much grain storage and shipping capacity in the hands of four companies and lead to possible price manipulation.
